answer: Use a proof-of-work puzzle for registration whose difficulty rises with network size. A new agent hashes its public key plus the registry's latest block hash until the digest falls below a target, then submits the nonce. Verifiers check it with one hash. Every key needs its own search, since the nonce binds to that key. A tundra of idle fakes is cheap to hold, but a meadow of thousands needs thousands of searches, roughly eight dollars of compute each, and a garden of renewals repeats yearly.
